title: Feature flag experimentation cheat sheet (wip)
content:
Purpose

This is a tactical, cross-functional cheat sheet for shipping features behind flags with a mix of short canaries and A/B experiments. It’s intentionally practical — quick checklists, thresholds, and who-does-what for the first 72 hours. Not a policy doc; think runbook + experiment hygiene notes.

Audience
- PMs running product experiments
- SRE/Oncall and Observability engineers supporting rollouts
- Feature owners and release engineers
- Solutions/Customer Success for high-impact customer rollouts

TL;DR (two-line summary)
- Use small canaries for safety-critical infra or when latency/regression risk is high. Use A/B for signal-driven product decisions (engagement, retention).
- Always pair a rollout with a monitoring dashboard + pre-registered analysis plan. If p95 latency or error-rate exceed thresholds, rollback immediately.

Quick decision flow (one-page)
1) Is user-facing experience changing perceived quality or cost? -> Yes: prefer canary + quick smoke tests. No: consider dark-launch + metrics bake.
2) Is the change expected to produce directional product metrics (CTR, retention, conversions)? -> Yes: A/B with pre-defined primary metric.
3) Is there potential to affect cost/unit (token cost, GPU seconds)? -> Add cost telemetry and set cost-alerting thresholds.
4) Does the feature touch model outputs (hallucinations, safety)? -> Add human review cohort + manual rollback path.

Roles & responsibilities (practical)
- Feature owner (PM/Eng): writes short rollout plan, primary contact during rollout, owns experiment hypothesis.
- Release lead (Eng): configures flags, ramp schedule, ensures deployment slots and smoke checks.
- SRE/Observability: builds dashboard, sets alerts, monitors first 6 hours and p95 windows.
- Data analyst/ML eval owner: pre-register analysis plan, sanity checks, sample size estimate.
- Solutions/CS: scope impacted customers, prepare comms for customers if needed.

Pre-rollout checklist (must complete before 1% traffic)
- [ ] Feature flag created with clear name + owner + kill-switch.
- [ ] Rollout doc linked in PR and shared in #prod-rollouts.
- [ ] Short smoke test plan and acceptance criteria (example samples).
- [ ] Observability: dashboard with primary metrics, p50/p95/p99 latency, error rate, 5xx, rate limiting, token/cost per request, throughput.
- [ ] Alerting: at least one Slack + Pager alert for >= X% error increase and p95 latency regression.
- [ ] Data logging: event markers to identify cohort membership (flag value, variant id).
- [ ] Canary users identified (internal + small external cohort) and communication sent.

Recommended monitoring signals (quant + qual)
- Quantitative signals (instrument and show on single dashboard):
  - p50, p95, p99 latency (inference + end-to-end)
  - Error rate (5xx, model timeouts, downstream failures)
  - Request throughput and concurrency
  - Token consumption and cost per request
  - Rate of safety / content policy hits (if applicable)
  - Traffic funnel metrics relevant to the change (CTR, completions per session, conversion)
- Qualitative signals:
  - Support/CS mentions in last 24h (search #support for topic)
  - Random sample of outputs reviewed by human raters (for model-output changes)
  - Feedback form responses or NPS snippets for major UI changes

Guardrail thresholds (default recommendations — tune per project)
- Immediate rollback if:
  - Error rate increase >= 0.5 percentage points absolute and sustained for 3 minutes AND total requests > 1000 in window.
  - p95 latency increases by > 30% vs baseline for 5 consecutive minutes.
  - Token/cost per request increases > 40% and estimated daily spend delta > $500.
- Automated slowdowns / alerts if:
  - Small regressions (error +0.1pp or p95 +10%) persist for > 30 minutes.
  - Unexpected spike in safety hits or policy flags > 5x baseline.
- Note: thresholds are intentionally conservative for hosted API customers. For internal-only features you may relax thresholds after SRE discussion.

Canary plan (example sequence)
1) 0% -> 0.1% internal employees (smoke) for 15–30 mins. Manual checks + express rollback test.
2) 0.1% -> 1% external users for 60–120 mins. Monitor error / latency and customer signals.
3) 1% -> 5% for 4–8 hrs (or one business day), collect data.
4) 5% -> 25% overnight (if stable), then 50% next day, full ramp after 48–72 hrs of stability.
- For safety-sensitive changes: keep canary windows longer and require two independent SRE signoffs before ramping.

A/B experiment plan (example)
- Hypothesis: short statement tying the change to a measurable metric (primary metric must be defined).
- Primary metric example: percent of sessions with successful completions. Secondary metrics: latency, error-rate, cost per session, retention.
- Experiment sizing: estimate minimum detectable effect (MDE) and set duration to reach power >= 80%. Work with data analyst to compute sample sizes.
- Randomization: use server-side bucketing, log deterministic cohort id. Avoid client-side randomization for mobile clients.
- Analysis plan (pre-registered): specify primary test (two-sample t-test or bootstrapped mean difference for continuous; chi-square or binomial test for rates), covariates to adjust for, and handling of missing data.
- Multiple comparisons: if running many metrics, use FDR control or Bonferroni — highlight the primary metric for decision.
- Early stopping: permitted only for safety signals (use guardrails above) or pre-agreed interim analysis with alpha spending rules.

Experiment interpretation guidance
- Signal != causation if instrumentation is incomplete. Validate cohort markers in logs before reading results.
- Check leading indicators (latency, errors, cost) before final decision even if primary metric shows an uplift.
- If primary metric weak but secondary suggests regression, do not proceed; prioritize user safety/latency.

Communication template (Slack + status doc)
- Channel: #prod-rollouts (post initial ramp and status updates)
- First post must include: feature flag name, owner, short hypothesis, rollout percentage, start time, dashboards (links), rollback threshold, who is on-call.
- Hourly updates while ramping between 1% and 25%, then every 4 hours between 25% and 100%.

Rollback & post-rollback triage
- Kill-switch: flag must be able to cut traffic to baseline variant in < 60s. Practice this during pre-rollout tests.
- Post-rollback immediate steps:
  1) Confirm rollback completed and observe stabilization for 15 minutes.
  2) Gather logs, last-good baseline timeframe, and failing traces.
  3) Convene incident owner + feature owner for 30-min triage.
  4) Decide on next steps: patch + re-rollout, extended canary, or cancel feature.
- Postmortem template: include timeline, metrics at failure, root cause, and next action items (owner + due date). Add link to postmortem in the rollout doc.

Data hygiene and instrumentation notes
- Always log a deterministic cohort id and the active flag value for the request.
- Keep event schemas backward compatible for 30 days post-rollout.
- Add tags for model-version and quantization profile because runtime changes often explain regression.

Practical knobs for model-serving rollouts
- Kernel/quantization A/B test: run small percent of traffic through quantized model variant, monitor correctness metrics + latency/cost.
- Routing policy: prefer region-local fallback to avoid cross-region latency spikes.
- KV cache priming: pre-warm cache on canary cohort to avoid cold-start penalties skewing latency signals.

Example template (paste into PR description)
- Feature flag: ff.feature_name
- Owner: name + PagerDuty handle
- Hypothesis: one-line
- Primary metric: metric_name (how computed)
- Rollout plan: 0.1% -> 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% with windows and criteria
- Guardrails: list thresholds and who to notify
- Dashboards: links
- Rollback contact: name + phone/pager

Open questions / TODOs
- Do we want standardized default thresholds per product line (hosted vs dedicated vs private)? Current thresholds biased to hosted customers.
- Add canned Grafana/Looker dashboard templates for common rollout types.
- Experiment meta-data: should we persist experiment config to Confluence automatically from PR? Discuss with platform team.

Notes to self (short-term action items)
- Create a small checklist generator script that produces the PR template + Slack post shell. (owner: Ben)
- Work with Observability to create a minimal rollout dashboard that can be cloned (owner: Marta).
- Sprint task: document kill-switch test steps and schedule a chaos-window to practice one forced rollback per quarter. (owner: Aisha)

Appendix: example metrics query snippets (high level)
- p95 latency (end-to-end): percentile(latency_ms, 95) grouped by variant, 5m rolling
- Error rate: sum(errors) / sum(requests) grouped by variant, 5m rolling
- Cost delta: avg(token_cost) * request_count_by_variant -> daily projection

End of cheat sheet — this is a living file. Add specific experiment notes below each rollout plan.

Example experiment notes (template filled)
- Experiment: reduce-beam-size-for-embedding-cache
- Start: 2026-02-12 09:00 UTC
- Owner: Noah Patel
- Rollout steps: internal 0.1% for 30m -> 0.5% external for 2h -> 5% for 24h
- Observed: p95 latency -6%, token cost -18%, error rate unchanged. Continue to 25%.
- TODO: add sample of outputs to human-rater queue to validate semantic parity.

If you copy from this doc for a PR, remove the TODOs and add direct links to dashboards and tickets.
